newsitem.title: JAPAN: JNOC signs east Siberia oil survey contract.
newsitem.headline: JNOC signs east Siberia oil survey contract.

text.p: The semi-governmental Japan National Oil Corp (JNOC) said on Tuesday it signed an agreement that will allow it to conduct a geological survey in Russia's gas-rich Irkutsk region.
The survey, due to take about one year, will be conducted in Irkutsk's Nepa-Botuobin area, in eastern Siberia, JNOC officials said.
The project's estimated cost of 260 million yen will be shouldered by JNOC, they said.

Industry sources have said that Japan is interested in taking part in developing energy resources in eastern Siberia as a means of alleviating its heavy reliance on the Middle East for gas and crude oil imports.
Japan imports about 80 percent of its crude oil from the Middle East.
